claims.text: The material family of interest is multiphase Ni-based superalloys containing gamma-prime precipitates.
The primary mechanical property of interest is tensile ductility, measured as elongation to failure.
Aging at 0.6–0.7 Tm produces a non-monotonic ductility response consisting of an initial decrease followed by recovery.
The non-monotonic ductility response is driven by evolution of gamma-prime interfaces from coherent through semi-coherent to incoherent states.
The change in interfacial coherency causes a transition from dislocation shearing to precipitate bypass.
The proposed initial alloy is a solution-treated and quenched Ni-Al-Ti-Cr-Mo superalloy containing a supersaturated solid solution.
The initial state contains a high density of nucleation sites for gamma-prime precipitation.
Increasing aging time increases gamma-prime precipitate size and alters precipitate-matrix coherency.
Small coherent gamma-prime precipitates are sheared by dislocations.
Shearing of small coherent precipitates promotes planar slip, localized deformation, high work hardening, and limited ductility.
As gamma-prime precipitates grow and lose coherency, dislocations bypass them by Orowan looping.
The transition to bypass initially causes a sharp ductility decrease through interfacial stress concentration.
At longer aging times, increased inter-particle spacing and stable semi-coherent interfaces promote homogeneous dislocation distributions and cross-slip.
More homogeneous dislocation distribution and cross-slip recover tensile ductility at long aging times.
The elongation-to-failure curve versus aging time is predicted to have a U or V shape.
The ductility minimum coincides with the critical precipitate size for the shearing-to-bypassing transition.
The non-monotonic transition occurs only at gamma-prime volume fractions of approximately 15–30%.
The transition is not expected at very low precipitate volume fractions or when precipitates are incoherent from the start.
Refractory additions such as Re or Ru can alter stacking-fault and interfacial energies and thereby shift the critical precipitate size.
The conventional baseline is a monotonic loss of ductility with aging due to precipitate coarsening and loss of matrix strength.

contradictions.description: The structural mediator labels Orowan looping as a shearing mechanism and Orowan bowing as bypassing, whereas the mechanism field identifies Orowan looping as bypass. Orowan bowing and loop formation are generally stages of precipitate bypass rather than precipitate shearing.

The hypothesis specifies a progression from coherent to semi-coherent to incoherent interfaces, but the proposed long-time recovery is attributed to formation of a stable semi-coherent interface after precipitates have already lost coherency. The intended long-time interfacial state is therefore inconsistent.
